 Fila Goes All in on Experiential Retail With Debut of a Full-size Pickleball Court Inside Lotte World Mall Store in South Korea
 In addition to Fila's first run specialty store, it also introduced Korea's first pickleball court integrated within a Fila retail store in Q3.

 Fila is expanding its presence in experiential sports retail.
 The footwear brand opened its first running-focused store, Fila Running Club, in Seoul in the Seoul Forest area in September. The brand in September also introduced Fila Pickleball Club at the Lotte World Mall, also in Seoul, which features Korea’s first pickleball court integrated within a Fila retail store.
 Fila operations is part of the Misto division of Misto Holdings. The South Korean company in April 2025 changed its name from Fila Holdings Corp. to Misto Holdings as it wanted to focus on its broader portfolio as a global brand management firm. In addition to Fila, Misto also manages the Titleist and FootJoy brands, among others. As part of that broader global focus, Misto also relocated company headquarters to the Cykan Tower in the Gangnam neighborhood of Seoul. It said it needed to “address growing demand for talent and office space driven by business expansion.”

 Misto on Monday said consolidated revenue for the third quarter ended Sept. 30, 2026, rose 3.4 percent year-over-year to 1.1 trillion won, while operating profit fell 3.0 percent to 128.0 billion won. For the nine months, consolidated revenue increased 8.2 percent year-over-year to 3.8 trillion won, while operating profit jumped to 616.9 billion won.

 For the Misto segment, which includes Fila operations, revenue was up 15.1 percent to 207.8 billion won and operating profit increased 8.6 percent to 9.4 billion won, both on a year-over-year basis. Misto highlighted double-digit year-over-year revenue growth in Malaysia, while the Korea business also “continued to build growth momentum, driven by the apparel category.”
 Misto said that in Greater China, the company continued to build on the solid growth of its core brands. It partnered with Mucent to open the Korean streetwear brand’s first store in Taiwan, with an additional physical store slated to open in December. “The company is also preparing further brand launches targeted for the Spring/Summer 2027 season as it continues to build long-term growth drivers in the region,” Misto said.
 For the Acushnet segment, third quarter revenue inched up 1.1 percent to 917.6 billion won, while operating profit was down 3.8 percent to 118.5 billion won, both on a year-over-year basis. Misto noted that FootJoy also saw improved profitability, driven by increased golf shoe sales. 
 “In the third quarter, we expanded our growth foundation by strengthening the competitiveness of our core businesses and diversifying our brand portfolio, while also achieving growth in both revenue and operating profit in the Misto segment,” said chief financial officer Ho Yeon “Aaron” Lee, in a statement. “Going forward, we will continue to strengthen our competitive advantages across business segments and enhance operational efficiency to drive sustainable growth.”
